headline: Chinese Coast Guard enters restricted waters near Taiwan-held Pratas
dek: Taiwan's Coast Guard said a Chinese Coast Guard ship entered restricted waters near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands (Dongsha) on Tuesday; its Taichung vessel was dispatched to warn it away; both sides broadcast messages — Chinese ship: 'the so-called Republic of China does not exist';…
sources: Taiwan Coast Guard (statement); Reuters reporting (Liz Lee, Ben Blanchard, Karen Lema)
fault_line: Salami-slicing or show of force — how far does Beijing push around Taiwan's coast guard before Taipei has to answer with more than radio broadcasts?

sections.what_happened: Taiwan's Coast Guard said a Chinese Coast Guard ship entered restricted waters near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands (Dongsha) on Tuesday; its Taichung vessel was dispatched to warn it away; both sides broadcast messages — Chinese ship: 'the so-called Republic of China does not exist'; Taiwanese ship: 'the Republic of China, Taiwan, is a sovereign and independent country'; standoff continuing at report time. Follows Taiwan's water-cannon use against a Chinese fishing boat near Pratas last week (China TAO: Taiwan must 'bear the consequences'). SEPARATE from the same-day Sabina Shoal event: Chinese Southern Theatre Command said USS Charleston 'illegally intruded' near Sabina Shoal early Tuesday and dispatched navy forces to track/monitor; US Navy no comment; last known US FONOP in SCS was >1yr ago. Philippines military spox rejected China's permission-requirement claim. At a Taipei forum Tuesday, US congressional review commission chair called Chinese coast-guard patrols east of Taiwan 'highly destabilising'; Taiwan NSC Sec-Gen Joseph Wu: China has no legal claim to waters off the island's east.
sections.what_verified: Reuters bylines across Straits Times, Times Live, BusinessWorld, Times Now, KWSN — consistent detail.
sections.what_disputed: No Chinese official response to the Pratas account at report time (TAO silent); Chinese version of the Sabina event is one-sided (US Navy no comment). Standoff status at end of day unknown — monitor.
sections.why_matters: Two flashpoints in one day: a US warship at Sabina Shoal, a Chinese coast-guard ship at Taiwan's Pratas. Map both on screen — the South China Sea is heating at both ends of the same waterway. TOTW stance: present both militaries' claims side by side; China's 'permission' doctrine gets the skeptical treatment.
sections.context: Background: NEW Pratas Islands standoff — Chinese Coast Guard enters restricted waters near Taiwan-held Pratas; simultaneous with Sabina Shoal FONOP

totw_analysis: Our read: Two flashpoints in one day: a US warship at Sabina Shoal, a Chinese coast-guard ship at Taiwan's Pratas. Map both on screen — the South China Sea is heating at both ends of the same waterway. TOTW stance: present both militaries' claims side by side; China's 'permission' doctrine gets the skeptical treatment.
